sbf.chart_title: RTS retail and F&B spending: annual base-case scenario
sbf.status: Scenario-based estimates, not observed outcomes or guaranteed forecasts
sbf.rounding_note: Use published approximately S$290m; rounded component values subtract to S$294m.
sbf.trip_warning: 51% is projected growth, not a share of people or spending.
sbf.period: Annual post-RTS scenario; pre-RTS spending comparator is 2025.
sbf.sample: March 2026 survey: about 1,700 Singapore and 400 Johor respondents. JB sample covers 2025 visitors and/or intended 2027 visitors; Singapore workers excluded.
sbf.method: Mastercard transactions, surveys, official statistics, consultations and travel/spending modelling.
sbf.caveat: Sensitive to adoption, trips, spending and substitution. Exchange rates, fares, macroeconomy and sentiment are not explicitly quantified; adaptation is incompletely captured. Net sector impact does not imply universal business decline.
sbf.evidence: Press-release opening paragraphs; factsheet Q1, Q3–9, Q14.

aci.publication: Song and Romzi, ACI Research Paper 06-2026, May 2026
aci.chart_title: Modelled corridor real-wage gains under distinct policy scenarios
aci.status: Counterfactual spatial-equilibrium simulations, not observed growth
aci.scenario_label: Both tables explicitly label results lower-bound scenarios.
aci.period_caution: Joint table explicitly says 2030; Table 1 itself does not print a horizon. Avoid an unqualified 2030 label on the standalone value.
aci.model: Singapore plus 13 Peninsular Malaysian regions, two sectors; calibrated from 2019. JS-SEZ starts 2025, RTS 2027; baseline fundamentals fixed.
aci.assumptions: Productivity benchmark +1.5%; RTS service-trade and migration costs -10%. Manufacturing trade-cost prose says benchmark -10%, but lower-bound robustness text says -5%; preserve this inconsistency.
aci.limitations: No explicit daily commuting, endogenous interregional capital or local housing markets; road-only trade.
aci.display_warning: 1.47% is a corridor average real-wage gain, not Singapore GDP growth. Keep separate from spending-flow estimates.
